sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导者，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、

sentences.en: Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、扎伊兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 您可以实时观看其中一些毫无保留、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Estet Herndon.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的埃斯特·赫恩登。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今日要闻。

sentences.en: In a leaked cable, the CIA made an explosive admission that the agency has lost dozens of informants to foreign enemies.
sentences.zh: 在一份泄露的电报中，中央情报局（CIA）承认了一个爆炸性事实：该机构已经损失了数十名外国线人。

sentences.en: My colleague, Julian Barnes, on why the failures happened and how the CIA got sloppy at its own game.
sentences.zh: 我的同事朱利安·巴恩斯将为您解析这些失败发生的原因，以及CIA是如何在自己的游戏中变得疏忽大意的。

sentences.en: It's Friday, October 8th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月8日，星期五。

sentences.en: Julian, can you tell me about this secret CIA message?
sentences.zh: 朱利安，你能跟我说说这份CIA的秘密电报吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Last week, the CIA sent a worldwide message to all of its stations and bases around the globe.
sentences.zh: 上周，CIA向其全球所有的站点和基地发送了一份全球通报。

sentences.en: So every place there is a CIA officer stationed, they got a copy of this relatively short but pretty explosive cable.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，每一个有CIA官员驻扎的地方，都收到了一份相对简短但内容相当劲爆的电报。

sentences.en: And the message was that there is a real problem with CIA informants being arrested, killed, or compromised.
sentences.zh: 电报的内容是，CIA的线人被捕、被杀或身份暴露的问题已经非常严重。

sentences.en: And what was unusual is this is usually, you know, the kind of information that's, you know, the most closely held secret.
sentences.zh: 不同寻常的是，这通常属于那种保密级别最高的信息。

sentences.en: So it sounds like the CIA's version of sending up a flare saying, we are acknowledging that we are losing our people.
sentences.zh: 所以这听起来像是CIA发出的求救信号，承认他们正在失去自己的情报人员。

sentences.en: Is that a fair way to characterize it?
sentences.zh: 这样描述准确吗？

sentences.en: That's a great way to characterize it.
sentences.zh: 这个描述非常贴切。

sentences.en: This was something where the CIA was trying to get the attention of its officers, its case officers who run informants, who develop sources, who collect the intelligence the U.S.
sentences.zh: CIA此举是为了引起其官员的注意，特别是那些负责管理线人、发展来源、收集美国所依赖情报的案件官员。

sentences.en: relies on.
sentences.zh: 他们依赖这些情报。

sentences.en: It wanted their attention.
sentences.zh: CIA需要他们的关注。

sentences.en: It wanted them to focus on it.
sentences.zh: 需要他们重视这个问题。

sentences.en: And it wanted it not to just be the sort of standard reminder, but get people's attention by being very specific about the scope of the problem.
sentences.zh: 而且这不仅仅是常规提醒，他们通过明确指出问题的严重程度来引起人们的警觉。

sentences.en: So what is the scope of that problem?
sentences.zh: 那么问题的严重程度究竟如何？

sentences.en: Well, we're talking about dozens of informants over several years that have been lost to the United
sentences.zh: 我们指的是过去几年里，美国损失了数十名线人。

sentences.en: States.
sentences.zh: “损失”可能意味着线人被捕，由于身陷海外监狱而无法再与美国联系。

sentences.en: And losing people can be an informant is arrested and no longer can talk to the United States because the source is now in a prison overseas.
sentences.zh: 也可能意味着线人被处决，因为许多国家会迅速处死那些被怀疑为美国充当间谍的人。

sentences.en: It also can mean that the source is executed, as many countries will promptly kill somebody suspected of being a spy for the United States.
sentences.zh: 还有第三种更复杂的情况。

sentences.en: And then there's a third, more complicated category.
sentences.zh: 这些人虽然仍在与美国联系，

sentences.en: And these people are still talking to the United
sentences.zh: 但美国无法确定他们是否已经倒戈。

sentences.en: States, but the U.S.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些线人已经失去了利用价值。

sentences.en: can't trust that they haven't been turned.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And so the informant is useless.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这几类人各自的比例吗？

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 是被捕的人多？

sentences.en: Do we know what the proportion of people who are in any of those categories?
sentences.zh: 还是死亡的人多？

sentences.en: Have more of them been arrested?
sentences.zh: 或者是倒戈的人多？

sentences.en: Have more of them died?
sentences.zh: 出于安全考虑，我们不便透露具体数字。

sentences.en: Or have more of them been turned?
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So we're not putting out specific numbers for security reasons.
sentences.zh: 但我们可以告诉你，占比最大的是双重间谍，也就是那些被怀疑已经倒戈的人。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: But we can tell you the biggest category is those double agents, the people who are in the suspected to be turned category.
sentences.zh: 那么朱利安，当你看到这份电报时，你的反应是什么？

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 我的反应是，这个问题比我们了解的要严重得多，CIA的间谍手段确实存在问题。

sentences.en: So Julian, when you saw the cable, what was your reaction?
sentences.zh: 也许系统内部出了什么差错。

sentences.en: My reaction was that this problem was bigger than we understood, that there were real problems with the CIA's spy craft.
sentences.zh: 如果真是这样，那事态就非常严重了。

sentences.en: Maybe there is something systemically wrong.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，美国依赖CIA及其人力情报来源来收集信息，以避免战争、冲突或缓和

sentences.en: And if that's the case, it's a really big deal.
sentences.zh: 国际关系，从而在理论上让美国更安全。

sentences.en: I mean, the United States relies on the CIA and relies on its human sources to collect the kind of information that we use to avoid war or avoid conflicts or smooth out
sentences.zh: 所以我的反应是，这是一件大事。

sentences.en: international relations to, you know, make the United States safer in theory.
sentences.zh: 如果美国正在失去优势，那问题就大了。

sentences.en: And so my reaction was this is a big deal.
sentences.zh: 我们对这份电报了解得越多，就越觉得它是在发出这种警告。

sentences.en: If the U.S.
sentences.zh: 出于某种原因，美国在世界各地招募间谍的能力已经下降了。

sentences.en: is losing its edge, that matters.
sentences.zh: 这种恶化是如何发生的？

sentences.en: And the more we learned about this cable, that seemed to be the kind of warning it was delivering.
sentences.zh: 我认为可以从两个大类来分析。

sentences.en: For some reason, the United States has gotten less good at recruiting spies around the world.
sentences.zh: 首先是世界形势的变化。

sentences.en: And how did that deterioration occur?
sentences.zh: 具体指哪方面？

sentences.en: Well, I think of it in two broad categories of what's going on here.
sentences.zh: 首先是技术方面，各类技术发生了翻天覆地的变化，

sentences.en: And the first is how the world has changed.
sentences.zh: 包括通信、人工智能、人脸识别等，这些技术让现代世界的间谍工作变得极其困难。

sentences.en: In what way?
sentences.zh: 等等，具体是什么样的？

sentences.en: Well, first and foremost, with technology, there is a dramatic change in all kinds of technology,
sentences.zh: 技术是如何影响间谍的行动能力的？

sentences.en: communications, artificial intelligence, facial recognition, some broad categories that make it really, really difficult to be a spy in the modern world.
sentences.zh: 让我们回想一下经典的间谍电影或小说。

sentences.en: Wait, what does that look like?
sentences.zh: 比如《红雀》系列小说，里面提到美国间谍在莫斯科与线人见面时，要花几个小时来

sentences.en: How has technology impacted the abilities for spies to operate?
sentences.zh: 摆脱克格勃或联邦安全局的跟踪，他们会做各种复杂的动作来甩掉尾巴，用CIA的术语来说就是“进入黑暗状态”。

sentences.en: Well, let's think back to classic spy movies or classic spy novels.
sentences.zh: 争取几分钟与线人独处，进行快速传递、死信投放，或者争取更多时间进行交谈。

sentences.en: You know, the Red Sparrow novels, they talk about American spies in Moscow going to meet a source, spending hours trying to
sentences.zh: 我想到了杰森·伯恩的画面。

sentences.en: elude the KGB or FSB tail, and that they were just doing all these elaborate moves to lose the tail, to go black in the parlance of the CIA.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是这样。

sentences.en: Get just a few minutes to be alone with the source and do a brush pass or do a dead drop or get a little bit more time and actually have a conversation.
sentences.zh: 杰森·伯恩和007那种只会炸毁更多东西的风格不同。

sentences.en: I'm getting Jason Bourne images.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Jason Bourne 007 blows more stuff up.
sentences.zh: 杰森·伯恩和007那种只会炸毁更多东西的风格不同。

sentences.en: But that classic spy tale.
sentences.zh: 但那只是经典的间谍故事。

sentences.en: The problem is, you can't do any of that.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，你根本做不到那些。

sentences.en: Jason Bourne has three passports, five passports,
sentences.zh: 杰森·伯恩有三本、五本护照，

sentences.en: 007 opens a drawer, takes out a new passport.
sentences.zh: 007打开抽屉，拿出一本新护照。

sentences.en: Well, guess what?
sentences.zh: 可你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: You go into a foreign country, they're going to scan your retina.
sentences.zh: 当你进入一个外国时，他们会扫描你的视网膜。

sentences.en: Like, you can't change your retina.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，你无法改变视网膜。

sentences.en: The whole three passports thing doesn't work anymore.
sentences.zh: 那种“三本护照”的把戏已经行不通了。

sentences.en: And, you know, walking around Beijing trying to lose the tail, there's cameras everywhere.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，在像北京这样的城市里想甩掉跟踪者，到处都是摄像头。

sentences.en: They're connected to the world's most powerful facial recognition and AI software that is identifying people.
sentences.zh: 它们连接着世界上最强大的面部识别和人工智能软件，能够精准识别每一个人。

sentences.en: And so this technological change means it's way, way harder to be a spy these days.
sentences.zh: 所以这种技术变革意味着，如今当间谍变得极其、极其困难。

sentences.en: With that constant surveillance in this Big Brother world that we now live in, is that the main way in which the landscape has changed around the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在这个我们所处的“老大哥”式全天候监控世界里，这是否是美国和中情局所面临的局势发生变化的主要方式？

sentences.en: and the CIA?
sentences.zh: 以及中情局？

sentences.en: That's an important way it's changed.
sentences.zh: 这确实是发生变化的一个重要方面。

sentences.en: But, you know, the other way it's changed is we have the development of some really, really good counterintelligence services in the world from places that weren't
sentences.zh: 但你知道，另一个变化是，世界上出现了一些非常、非常厉害的反间谍机构，它们来自那些以前

sentences.en: always thought of as having the best spy services, right?
sentences.zh: 并不被认为拥有顶尖间谍服务的国家，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, classically, you know, the KGB and the successor organizations, the SVR and the FSB were the great spies and the great spy hunters.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，传统上，克格勃及其继任组织——俄罗斯对外情报局（SVR）和联邦安全局（FSB）——才是伟大的间谍和间谍猎手。

sentences.en: But it's not just Russia anymore that is really good at this.
sentences.zh: 但现在，擅长此道的不仅仅是俄罗斯了。

sentences.en: Iran has some of the best counterintelligence operations there are.
sentences.zh: 伊朗拥有目前世界上最顶尖的反间谍行动能力。

sentences.en: They have destroyed the American network inside that country.
sentences.zh: 他们摧毁了美国在该国境内的情报网。

sentences.en: Pakistan, turns out, is really, really good at finding American informants.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，巴基斯坦在揪出美国线人方面也非常、非常在行。

sentences.en: And time and time again, they have broken down our networks, penetrated our networks, turned our sources.
sentences.zh: 他们一次又一次地瓦解了我们的网络，渗透了我们的网络，策反了我们的线人。

sentences.en: And those turned sources feed us bad information.
sentences.zh: 而那些被策反的线人会向我们提供虚假情报。

sentences.en: And that leads to bad intelligence.
sentences.zh: 这导致了错误的情报判断。

sentences.en: So we cannot just assume that the traditional powers are the only ones who know how to do this.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不能理所当然地认为，只有传统强国才懂得这些手段。

sentences.en: And we really need to understand that other countries are getting better at this and maybe better than we are.
sentences.zh: 我们必须清醒地认识到，其他国家正在变得越来越强，甚至可能比我们更强。

sentences.en: Well, if they're getting better, doesn't that put more pressure on the United States to also match that, to also be at the top of its game?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果他们变得更强了，这是否会给美国带来更大压力，要求我们也要迎头赶上，保持顶尖水平？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely it does.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: But the reality of the situation is that the CIA has gotten sloppy.
sentences.zh: 但现实情况是，中情局已经变得松懈了。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: Okay, Julian, you said that the CIA got sloppy.
sentences.zh: 好的，朱利安，你说中情局变得松懈了。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 这是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, that kind of leads us to the second big category of what went wrong.
sentences.zh: 这正好引出了导致失败的第二个大类原因。

sentences.en: We let our spy craft slip.
sentences.zh: 我们让自己的间谍技术退步了。

sentences.en: And you have to remember the wider context here.
sentences.zh: 你必须记住这里更宏观的背景。

sentences.en: You know, what has the CIA been doing over the last 20 years?
sentences.zh: 你知道，过去20年里中情局都在忙些什么？

sentences.en: They've been fighting terrorism.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在反恐。

sentences.en: That's what the focus of the United States was.
sentences.zh: 这就是美国工作的重心。

sentences.en: After 9-11, counterterrorism became the most important issue.
sentences.zh: 9·11事件后，反恐成了最重要的议题。

sentences.en: The war in Afghanistan, the war in
sentences.zh: 阿富汗战争、

sentences.en: Iraq, the war in Syria, the threat of al-Qaeda, the threat of Islamic State.
sentences.zh: 伊拉克战争、叙利亚战争，还有基地组织和伊斯兰国的威胁。

sentences.en: And, you know, it turns out that it's actually a different thing to try to collect information against another country,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，事实证明，试图针对另一个国家收集情报，与针对恐怖组织收集情报是两码事，

sentences.en: another country that operates its own counterintelligence service, that is watching for
sentences.zh: 因为那个国家拥有自己的反间谍机构，时刻防范着

sentences.en: spies, has got a whole group of people trying to catch spies, and has kind of huge resources to try to counter the CIA.
sentences.zh: 间谍，有一整套人马专门负责抓间谍，并拥有巨大的资源来对抗中情局。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: How is it that collecting information against another country is different or harder than against some of these terrorism organizations that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 为什么针对另一个国家收集情报，会比针对美国一直关注的那些恐怖组织（比如ISIS）更困难或有所不同？

sentences.en: has been focusing on, you know, groups like ISIS?
sentences.zh: 你知道，像ISIS这样的组织？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, ISIS probably is looking for moles.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，ISIS可能也在寻找内鬼。

sentences.en: They're probably trying to figure out what of their people are loyal to them.
sentences.zh: 他们可能也在试图弄清楚哪些人对自己忠诚。

sentences.en: But they don't have the same means to monitor people, right?
sentences.zh: 但他们没有同样的手段去监控人员，对吧？

sentences.en: That is not something that al-Qaeda or the Islamic State in most cases have the ability to do.
sentences.zh: 在大多数情况下，基地组织或伊斯兰国并不具备这种能力。

sentences.en: I mean, if you are a nation state, you can listen to phone calls in your country.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你是一个主权国家，你可以监听国内的电话。

sentences.en: You can listen to phone calls in other countries.
sentences.zh: 你可以监听其他国家的电话。

sentences.en: You can follow cell phones.
sentences.zh: 你可以追踪手机信号。

sentences.en: And so, you know, protecting informants, developing informants inside a potentially adversarial country requires more care.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，在潜在的敌对国家境内保护线人、发展线人，需要更加谨慎。

sentences.en: It requires extra layers of protection.
sentences.zh: 这需要额外的保护层。

sentences.en: It requires teaching your informants to be spies, right?
sentences.zh: 这需要教会你的线人如何成为间谍，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It sounds like you're saying that the muscles that the CIA developed during the Cold War era,
sentences.zh: 听起来你的意思是，中情局在冷战时期培养出的那些“肌肉”，

sentences.en: that they became synonymous with, that spy craft and counterintelligence, that they may have lost some of that when they started focusing so much on counterterrorism.
sentences.zh: 那些让他们引以为傲的间谍技术和反间谍能力，在他们开始过度关注反恐时，可能已经丧失了一些。

sentences.en: Is that the main way the CIA sort of let its spy craft slip?
sentences.zh: 这是中情局让间谍技术退步的主要方式吗？

sentences.en: Or is there another?
sentences.zh: 还是有其他原因？

sentences.en: That's one way.
sentences.zh: 这只是其中之一。

sentences.en: The other way is kind of a subset of that, of mission over security.
sentences.zh: 另一个原因是前者的一个子集，即“任务重于安全”。

sentences.en: What's that mean?
sentences.zh: 那是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, it's kind of like quantity over quality.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这有点像“重数量轻质量”。

sentences.en: Maybe that's a way to think about it.
sentences.zh: 也许可以这样理解。

sentences.en: You know, if you're a CIA case officer, those are the people who go overseas and recruit new informants.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你是一名中情局外勤官员，也就是那些去海外招募新线人的人，

sentences.en: You know, former officials tell us the way you get promoted is you bring in new sources and
sentences.zh: 前官员告诉我们，晋升的方式就是带回新的情报来源，

sentences.en: you would have a successful tour if you developed 10 new sources, you know, three in the Ministry of
sentences.zh: 如果你能发展10个新线人，比如在国防部发展3个，

sentences.zh: 在中央银行发展2个，还有3个关系广泛的商人，那你的任期就算圆满成功。

sentences.en: But what experts have told us is, you know, quantity is great.
sentences.zh: 但专家告诉我们，数量固然好，

sentences.en: And you have to, instead of focusing on the numbers, you have to take the extra time to do the vetting, to make sure the people you are
sentences.zh: 所以你不能只盯着数字，必须花额外的时间进行背景审查，确保你招募的人是

sentences.en: recruiting really are on the side of the United States, really are working to help the CIA develop

sentences.en: its information and not double agents, not people working for the adversarial country.

sentences.en: There is a classic example that former officials will say that is the sort of worst case scenario.
sentences.zh: 有一个经典案例，前官员们常说那是某种最坏的情况。

sentences.en: In 2009, the CIA was recruiting a Jordanian doctor to infiltrate al-Qaeda, to collect information and bring it back to the United States.

sentences.en: They arranged for that doctor to go to the secret base that the CIA operated in Afghanistan, Camp Chapman in coast Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 他们安排那名医生前往中情局在阿富汗运营的秘密基地，即阿富汗霍斯特省的查普曼营地。

sentences.en: They were so eager to meet the source, to hear what he had to say, and not offend the source to keep on their good side, that the security checks, the pat-downs were lax.
sentences.zh: 他们当时太急于见到线人，想听听他要说什么，为了不冒犯线人以维持良好关系，结果安全检查和搜身都非常松懈。

sentences.en: The person got into the base to meet with the CIA agent,
sentences.zh: 那个人进入基地与中情局特工会面，

sentences.en: Al-Qaeda had turned that person.

sentences.en: The person was now working for Al-Qaeda.
sentences.zh: 那个人现在是在为基地组织工作。

sentences.en: He had become a suicide bomber, set off the bomb, seven agency officers were killed.
sentences.zh: 他成了一名自杀式炸弹袭击者，引爆了炸弹，七名中情局官员丧生。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: It was one of the most devastating days in CIA history.
sentences.zh: 那是中情局历史上最惨痛的日子之一。

sentences.en: And, you know, former officials say a classic example of mission over security.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，前官员们说这是任务重于安全的典型案例。

sentences.en: The risks of a turned informant can be catastrophic in ways you can't really imagine.
sentences.zh: 被策反的线人所带来的风险，其灾难性程度是你无法想象的。

sentences.en: And that is why it is so important to take the painful steps and to always keep security at the forefront of your mind.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么采取那些痛苦的步骤，并始终将安全放在首位是如此重要。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: This is the exact type of tragedy that the cable points to.
sentences.zh: 这正是那份电报所指出的那种悲剧。

sentences.en: The real risk that comes with this type of spycraft.
sentences.zh: 这种间谍活动所带来的真正风险。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And despite those risks, the human asset is still really important to the CIA.
sentences.zh: 尽管存在这些风险，人力资源对中情局来说仍然非常重要。

sentences.en: The kind of intelligence you get from another person is really important.
sentences.zh: 你从另一个人那里获得的情报非常重要。

sentences.en: And it is information that you can't always get from a stolen document or an intercepted phone call.
sentences.zh: 而且这些信息是你无法总是从被窃取的文件或被拦截的电话中获取的。

sentences.en: Is there an example when this type of intelligence outweighed the human risk?
sentences.zh: 有没有这种情报超过人力风险的例子？

sentences.en: There's one really important example, and that is the 2016 election and Russian interference.
sentences.zh: 有一个非常重要的例子，那就是2016年大选和俄罗斯的干预。

sentences.en: And one of the key findings that the CIA made was that Vladimir Putin favored Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 中情局得出的关键结论之一是弗拉基米尔·普京偏向唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: This was, as you'll recall, a controversial finding.
sentences.zh: 正如你所记得的，这是一个有争议的结论。

sentences.en: Not all Republicans agreed with that.
sentences.zh: 并非所有共和党人都同意这一点。

sentences.en: They felt that Russia was just trying to cause chaos.
sentences.zh: 他们认为俄罗斯只是想制造混乱。

sentences.en: But it turns out that the reason the CIA knew about that, in part, was a human source.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，中情局之所以知道这一点，部分原因是一名人力线人。

sentences.en: They had somebody who was in some meetings with Putin.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个人参加了普京的一些会议。

sentences.en: And Vladimir Putin doesn't use cell phones.
sentences.zh: 而弗拉基米尔·普京不使用手机。

sentences.en: He doesn't let a lot of documents get created with his thinking on them.
sentences.zh: 他不让太多包含他想法的文件被创建出来。

sentences.en: It's really hard to understand his intentions, his thinking.
sentences.zh: 要了解他的意图和想法真的很难。

sentences.en: And the way to do that is to get sources close to him.
sentences.zh: 而做到这一点的方法就是找到接近他的人。

sentences.en: People who have been in meetings with him have heard him talk with advisors.
sentences.zh: 那些曾与他开会并听到他与顾问交谈的人。

sentences.en: And this asset was really important to the CIA making that judgment.
sentences.zh: 而这个资产对于中情局做出这一判断非常重要。

sentences.en: Now, that asset was also an example of someone who was loSt. In this case, though, the CIA extracted that operative from Russia and brought him to Northern Virginia to make sure he
sentences.zh: 现在，那个资产也是一个失去联系的例子。不过在这种情况下，中情局将那名特工从俄罗斯撤出，并带到了北弗吉尼亚，以确保他

sentences.en: didn't get caught, to make sure he didn't get turned.
sentences.zh: 没有被抓，确保他没有被策反。

sentences.en: So, I can see how this shows the value of that human intelligence.
sentences.zh: 所以，我能看出这如何体现了那种人力情报的价值。

sentences.en: But if the CIA has already been so sloppy, and we've lost a number of spies to these countries as a result, what happens if the CIA is
sentences.zh: 但如果中情局已经如此草率，导致我们因此失去了许多间谍，如果中情局

sentences.en: not successful in reshifting its focus to protecting these human assets?
sentences.zh: 不能成功地将其重心重新调整到保护这些人力资产上，会发生什么？

sentences.en: I mean, that's an interesting question, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个有趣的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Because what would happen if all the human sources dried up or went away?
sentences.zh: 因为如果所有的人力线人都枯竭或消失了，会发生什么？

sentences.en: What if we were just dependent on the information we can get from spy satellites and intercepted phone calls?
sentences.zh: 如果我们只是依赖从间谍卫星和拦截电话中获取的信息会怎样？

sentences.en: We wouldn't be completely blind.
sentences.zh: 我们不会完全变成瞎子。

sentences.en: But I think what the CIA would tell you is, if we don't get this right, we'll lose some nuance.
sentences.zh: 但我认为中情局会告诉你，如果我们不把这件事做好，我们就会失去一些细微差别。

sentences.en: And in intelligence, nuance is really important.
sentences.zh: 而在情报工作中，细微差别非常重要。

sentences.en: And when we get the nuance wrong, we make bad policy decisions.

sentences.en: So, I think if we had Bill Burns on here with us, the director of the CIA, he would tell you, you know, we're going to make
sentences.zh: 所以，我想如果比尔·伯恩斯（中情局局长）和我们在一起，他会告诉你，你知道，我们会

sentences.en: sure we get this right, and we continue to develop these networks, and we will find a way to do it.

sentences.en: This question might seem out of left field, but is it clear that when the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这个问题可能看起来有点突兀，但当美国

sentences.en: has more spies out there, that if Bill Burns were here and said, we're going to do better on this front, that it's causational that the world will then be safer?

sentences.en: How do we know that the security vision that the CIA is pitching here is actually a good one?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么知道中情局在这里推销的安全愿景实际上是一个好的愿景？

sentences.en: Um, that's a pretty deep question.

sentences.zh: 我们知道中国人正在尽其所能窃取我们的技术秘密，以了解我们正在做的事情。

sentences.zh: 而且它可能会从
